extracted.intended_audience: administrative law scholars, judges, law students, and regulatory policy analysts
extracted.subtask_description: Scholarly analysis of how administrative agencies choose among distinct policymaking forms (rulemaking, adjudication, interpretations/guidance), how courts review those choices, and the normative implications of that choice for administrative law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policymaking tools available to agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: An administrative agency delegated some task ... might carry out that obligation by adopting a rule, bringing or deciding a case, or announcing its interpretation of the statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples enumerated: promulgating rules (rulemaking), bringing or deciding cases (adjudication), and issuing statutory interpretations or guidance. The article treats these as distinct policymaking forms that agencies are typically authorized to use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance of the choice among policymaking forms
rubrics_metrics.description: The significance of the choice among them, and the varying choices that agencies make.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The choice of form matters for legal and practical consequences; agencies vary in which tools they rely on. The Article emphasizes identifying and evaluating that significance as a central task.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial reaction: hands-off approach to agency forum choice
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency can choose among its available policymaking tools and a court will not require it to provide an explanation for its choice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characterized as 'hands-off' review; courts generally do not demand justification when an agency selects one policymaking form over another. The Article flags this as a distinctive feature of current judicial review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Puzzle: courts treat forum choice differently from other agency discretion
rubrics_metrics.description: This judicial reaction ... is perplexing because it is out of step with the rest of the law of judicial review of agency action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Article frames the discrepancy as a puzzle to be explained—why courts defer to forum choice when they scrutinize other discretionary agency decisions more closely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination and dismissal of possible reasons for deference
rubrics_metrics.description: This Part examines possible reasons why courts might treat agency choices of procedure differently than other exercises of discretion, but dismisses each of them as implausible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Article surveys candidate explanations for judicial hands-off treatment and finds them insufficient; while the page does not list the specific reasons, it signals a critical analytic review of standard justifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Courts' indirect control by adjusting consequences of forum choice
rubrics_metrics.description: Courts have a surprising degree of control over the consequences of an agency's choice of form. By adjusting the consequences of choosing one form or another, courts have the opportunity to respond to whatever concerns they might have about an agency's choice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key claim: rather than directly policing forum choice, courts can alter the legal effects attached to a chosen form (e.g., through doctrines of deference, remedies, standards of review), thereby providing a roundabout form of review. The Article treats this as the explanatory account for judicial behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need to notice and normatively address forum choice
rubrics_metrics.description: After noticing them, though, the next step is to come to terms with them. Part III of the Article starts that task.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Article moves from description and diagnosis to normative engagement—evaluating how the law should regard agency forum choice and recommending how doctrine or practice might respond. The page indicates substantive normative analysis will follow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirical/variational observation: agencies differ in reliance on forms
rubrics_metrics.description: The varying choices that agencies make.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Article documents that different agencies (and perhaps the same agency at different times) rely on different mixes of rulemaking, adjudication, and interpretive guidance—an empirical dimension relevant to assessing doctrinal responses.
